newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 6.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Thursday's Daily Variety:

* HOLLYWOOD - Veteran ICM TV agent Bob Sanitsky is leaving the agency after six years to lead a huge expansion by Dutch media conglomerate Polygram into the domestic TV business. Sanitsky, who is vice president and head of syndication and cable at International Creative Management, will now become president of the newly formed Polygram TV division.

* NEW YORK - The Bubble Factory is close to deals with "First Wives Club" stars Diane Keaton and Goldie Hawn to reteam in the comedy "Living Legends." A deal is expected to be sealed shortly. A source said the Bubble Factory committed $10 million in salaries for the two actresses to be split between them.

* LAS VEGAS - The theatrical life of a Hollywood film is shrinking because in the last six years the number of wide releases has grown at a faster rate than new screens, according to figures released at a ShoWest panel discussion Wednesday. As a result, the opening week of an average picture accounted for 32 percent of a film's total theatrical gross in 1996, compared with 24 percent in 1990, EDI president Marcie Polier said during the discussion.

* HOLLYWOOD - Time Warner's Warner Bros soundtrack for Howard Stern's movie, "Private Parts" was the top-selling album for the week ending March 2, with nearly 177,590 copies crossing retail registers, according to label executives.

* HOLLYWOOD - Sony's Columbia Tristar Television has a deal with the WB netlet for its new animated series "Men in Black," which is based on the Columbia Pictures-Amblin Entertainment summer theatrical starring Tommy Lee Jones and Will Smith.
